title: Testing and Evaluation of Large Language Models: Correctness, Non-Toxicity, and Fairness

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework, which generates Yes-No, Choice, and Wh-questions from combinations of gender groups and biased properties to calculate absolute and relative bias rates.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework, which generates Yes-No, Choice, and Wh-questions from combinations of racial groups and biased properties to calculate absolute and relative bias rates.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework, which generates Yes-No, Choice, and Wh-questions from combinations of religious groups and biased properties to calculate absolute and relative bias rates.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework, which generates Yes-No, Choice, and Wh-questions from combinations of age groups and biased properties to calculate absolute and relative bias rates.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework under the 'Ability' attribute, measuring absolute and relative bias rates toward individuals with disabilities using template-based and rule-based questions.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework under the 'Profession' attribute, measuring absolute and relative bias rates across different jobs and occupations.
Evaluated using the BiasAsker framework under the 'Body' attribute, calculating bias rates towards groups based on physical traits like weight or body shape.

Evaluated using the XCulturalBench framework by querying models across 10 languages about concrete cultural objects (e.g., holidays, songs) and abstract values to measure English/Western cultural dominance using an 'In-Culture Score' and Euclidean distance.
Evaluated as part of abstract cultural objects using the multilingual Political Coordinates Test (PCT) to measure the model's political and socioeconomic beliefs across different language queries.
